title: RoDAS: Evidence-Linked Decision Annotations for Sidewalk Robot Navigation
abstract: Outdoor mobile robots must interpret traffic rules and implicit social conventions when deciding whether to proceed, slow down, or yield. We introduce RoDAS (Robot Decision Annotation Schema) and a pipeline that uses vision-language models (VLMs) to generate evidence-linked annotations from raw sidewalk and crosswalk robot logs. The schema links critical scene components, explicit decision conditions, four-axis actions, and component-referenced Chain-of-Causation (CoC) explanations. The pipeline aligns route instructions, traffic-light information, front-camera observations, and wheel odometry, then generates and checks annotations in stages. We apply it to 74,359 keyframes and compare decision-only training with explanations learned as auxiliary targets or generated before decisions across five VLM backbones. On Cosmos-Reason2-8B, decision-only fine-tuning raises three-axis exact match from 39.55% to 69.04% on held-out places. Auxiliary supervision provides no established gain over decision-only training on this backbone. Replacing training explanations with those from other scenes with different decision conditions, while retaining action labels, leaves auxiliary-model accuracy nearly unchanged after retraining despite reduced agreement between generated explanations and recorded evidence. The linked records reveal errors near recorded label changes and subtle temporal, spatial, and motion-magnitude distinctions in action labels. For decision-only models of the same backbone, three-seed mean exact match is 50.6% near label changes versus 76.1% in stable regions. RoDAS supports the study of explanation–decision consistency and the diagnosis of both prediction failures and ambiguous action annotations.
contributions: A staged VLM pipeline aligns multimodal robot logs and records scene components, four-axis decisions, their governing conditions, and component-linked explanations.
Fine-tuning improves decision and component prediction. Decision-only, inline, and auxiliary supervision are compared across five VLM backbones.
Linked records expose errors near observed label changes, under different decision conditions, and on uncommon actions, while separating decision correctness from explanation agreement.
